subject: Re: R package nat, difficulties recognising mesh data

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: R package nat, difficulties recognising mesh data
parts:
Dear Alexander,

Can you try the read.hxsurf function? In spite of appearances, the amiramesh format is Amira’s general purpose format normally used for eg volumetric image data, not surfaces. 

The Surfaces section of the nat function reference may be helpful 

http://natverse.org/nat/reference/index.html

Best,

Greg. 


Sent from my iPhone

On 11 Mar 2020, at 17:54, Alexander Tinius <alex....@utoronto.ca> wrote:

Dear Dr. Jefferis,

I hope this message finds you in good health, and void of current
pandemic infections.

For one of our projects we are trying to import Amira surface meshes
into R, and your package 'nat' appears perfect for this purpose.
However, none of our Amira-meshes will import through any of the
function offered. I would be grateful, if you could offer any assistance
in bridging this problem. Neither Github nor stackoverflow seem to offer
any advice in this matter.

Best Regards,

Alex.

Surface meshes were created in Amira. The output from R (v3.6.3) reads
as follows:

amiratype("taylori-320889-cranium.surf", bytes = NULL)
[1] "HxSurface"
is.amiramesh("taylori-320889-cranium.surf")
[1] FALSE
meshinfo<-read.amiramesh.header("taylori-320889-cranium.surf", Parse
= TRUE, Verbose = FALSE)
Error in while (substring(t <- readLines(con, 1), 1, 2) != "@1") { :
  argument is of length zero
In addition: Warning message:
In readLines(con, 1) :
  incomplete final line found on 'taylori-320889-cranium.surf'
mesh1<-read.amiramesh("taylori-320889-cranium.surf",sections =
NULL,header = FALSE,simplify = FALSE,endian = NULL,ReadByteAsRaw =
FALSE,Verbose = FALSE)
Warning message:
In read.amiramesh("taylori-320889-cranium.surf", sections = NULL, :
  taylori-320889-cranium.surf does not appear to be an AmiraMesh file

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: R package nat, difficulties recognising mesh data
parts:
Dear Alex,

OK then it is likely that your file is a *binary* format HyperSurface. I have experimental support for reading these, but it is not yet in the released version of nat. You can resave your file in ASCII format from Amira (simpler for now if possible). If you send me a sample file off list I will test it against the experimental code for binary surfaces and try to release that soon.

All the best,

Greg.
